, for the MC/PCS networks, the exponential assumption for the call holding time is not appropriate, since it results in the under estimation of the blocking probability, which in turn leads to the actual system being more heavily loaded than that designed using the exponential assumption for holding time.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, when cell residence times follow general (nonlatticed) distributions, a general formula for handoff rate is obtained, and the exponential approximation is no longer valid.

, for mobile computing applications, the exponential assumption for the cell residence times results in an overestimation of the channel occupancy times, and hence, an underestimation of the handoff rate.
, when the call arrival process is Poisson, the cell residence time distribution has a significant impact on the performance of the MC/PCS networks.
